title: Machine learning identifies regional low-magnitude seismic unrest before the Ridgecrest and Anchorage earthquakes
summary: A random-forest method using statistical features from earthquake catalogs identified abnormal low-magnitude seismicity spreading across roughly 15–25% of Southern California and Southcentral Alaska up to about three months before the 2019 Ridgecrest sequence and 2018 Anchorage M7.1 earthquake. Finite-element mechanics models were used to propose a pore-fluid-pressure explanation. This is a retrospective analysis of two target events, not a demonstrated reliable warning system.
ai_technology: Random-forest machine-learning algorithm with earthquake-catalog statistical features
organization: Institute of Geophysics, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC); University of Edinburgh

evidence.tested: A random-forest method using statistical features from earthquake catalogs identified abnormal low-magnitude seismicity spreading across roughly 15–25% of Southern California and Southcentral Alaska up to about three months before the 2019 Ridgecrest sequence and 2018 Anchorage M7.1 earthquake.
evidence.unknown: The study analyzes two retrospective target events and explicitly notes that earthquake precursors remain ambiguous and reliable alert systems are not established. The pore-pressure mechanism is proposed from modeling rather than directly measured, and the finding is not prospective validation.
evidence.ai_role: Detected regional nonlinear patterns in low-magnitude seismic catalogs that the authors report as precursory unrest before two large earthquake sequences; the AI analysis identified the statistical pattern, while finite-element models supported a proposed mechanism.
